text:
ROOT_CAUSE: The current PHONE regex overly matches 10-digit numbers (like order numbers) because it does not require international country codes, punctuation separators, or preceding contact context, causing massive false positives.
RULE: The PHONE pattern must require either an explicit international prefix (+1, +44, +91) or strict phone punctuation/separators (dashes, dots, parentheses, or spaces between digit groups) to avoid matching 10-digit order numbers.
NEXT_EDIT: Refine the PHONE regex pattern to mandate standard phone separators or international country codes while retaining support for all required formats (intl_uk, paren, intl_in, dot, dash, plus1, bare, space).
ACTION: KEEP_GOING
